description: The hyperbolic metric density sigma_Omega(z) in a simply connected domain Omega is intimately connected to the Bloch constant. The key inequality sigma_Omega(z) >= 1/(2*R_Omega) bounds the metric from below. Eremenko's work on the hyperbolic metric of lattice complements connects the Landau constant to elliptic function theory and accessory parameters of the Lame equation.
mathematical_formalization: The hyperbolic metric ds = sigma_Omega(z)|dz| satisfies Delta log sigma_Omega = sigma_Omega^2 (Liouville equation). For f: D -> Omega univalent: sigma_Omega(f(z))|f'(z)| = sigma_D(z) = 1/(1-|z|^2). The Bloch radius: B_f = sup_{z in D} |f'(z)|(1-|z|^2)/2 * inf_{w in f(D)} 1/sigma_{f(D)}(w). For lattice complements: sigma relates to Weierstrass functions via the Lame equation.
analogical_connections: Hyperbolic metric density ~ information-theoretic Fisher information
Accessory parameters ~ moduli of Riemann surfaces
implementation_hypothesis: Compute the hyperbolic metric density numerically for candidate extremal domains using the Schwarz-Pick lemma and boundary element methods. For lattice complements, use the connection to elliptic functions. Compute sigma_Omega to high precision and extract the Bloch radius. Compare different domain classes (strips, slit disks, lattice complements).
experiment_seed: For the complement of the hexagonal lattice (normalized to inradius 1), compute sigma_Omega using Weierstrass P-function. Determine inf_w sigma_Omega(w) and the resulting Bloch constant bound. Repeat for square, triangular, and deformed lattices. Plot sigma_Omega as a heat map.
